messages.subject: data with different right-censored values
parts:
I have a dataset that includes a predictor variable with points that have different upper limits where I want to apply a linear regression model. In
this case I could not apply the censored data models from the Stan documentation that have a signle left or right-censored variable for the whole data.
Should I define these upper limits for each censored data point in the data or parameters block? Is there any example, either in Stan or JAGS where data points are allowed to have different upper or lower limit values?

Best,
Miguel

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: data with different right-censored values
parts:
On Tuesday, November 17, 2015 at 12:23:33 PM UTC-5, Miguel de Val-Borro wrote:
I have a dataset that includes a predictor variable with points that have different upper limits where I want to apply a linear regression model. In
this case I could not apply the censored data models from the Stan documentation that have a signle left or right-censored variable for the whole data.
Should I define these upper limits for each censored data point in the data or parameters block? Is there any example, either in Stan or JAGS where data points are allowed to have different upper or lower limit values?

Writing everything out in terms of N scalars is usually a last resort. This best way to do this in Stan is to do something like

data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  vector<lower=0>[N] upper_bound;
  ...
}
parameters{
  vector<lower=0,upper=1>[N] gamma; // you do not care about this directly
  ...
}
transformed parameters {
  vector<lower=0> theta;
  theta <- gamma .* upper_bound; // this is what you care about
  // and theta bounded between 0 and upper bound for each observation
}
model {
  // likelihood involving theta
  // prior on theta will result in Jacobian warnings from parser
  // but the partial derivative of theta[i] wrt gamma[i] is just a constant upper_bound[i]
  // so you can ignore the warning in this case
}

If the upper bounds were unknown parameters that varied across observations then it would be essential to do the Jacobian adjustment yourself in the model block.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: data with different right-censored values
parts:
On Tuesday, November 17, 2015 at 4:52:09 PM UTC-5, Miguel de Val-Borro wrote:
My predictor variable is in logarithmic scale so it does not really have a lower bound. In this case I will define it as:

vector[N] theta;

OK, in that case the declaration for gamma in parameters shouldn't have a lower bound. Or you could do it the original way with

theta <- log(gamma) + log_upper_bound;

Ben

My predictor variable is in logarithmic scale so it does not really have a lower bound. In this case I will define it as:

vector[N] theta;

OK, in that case the declaration for gamma in parameters shouldn't have a lower bound. Or you could do it the original way with

theta <- log(gamma) + log_upper_bound;

I would like to have a half-gaussian prior for these upper limits with an upper boundary given by each individual limit:

data {                                                                                  
    int<lower=1> n_limit;        // number of upper limits                              
    vector[n_limit] x_limit;     // predictor variable  upper limits                    
    ...                                                                                  
}                                                                                        
parameters {                                                                            
    vector<upper=x_limit>[n_limit] xtrue_limit; // x true values                        
    ...                                                                                  
}                                                                                        
model {                                                                                  
    xtrue_limit ~ normal(x_limit, 1);                                                    
    ...                                                                                  
}

But this does not work because the upper parameter for a vector has to be a scalar. Is there a way to define a half-normal distribution with a loop over the limits
instead of using an upper bound constraint?

Miguel


Miguel

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: data with different right-censored values
parts:
You'll have to do the offset by hand:

parameters {
vector<upper=0>[n_limit] xtrue_limit_raw; // x true values

transformed parameters {
vector[n_limit] xtrue_limit;
x_true_limit <- x_true_limt_raw + x_limit;

It's a constant Jacobian so you can just use x_true_limit as you
would have done before.

- Bob
